newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy far right to retract telecom bill amendments.
newsitem.headline: Italy far right to retract telecom bill amendments.

text.p: The far-right National Alliance (AN) party is withdrawing its amendments designed to obstruct a bill to create a regulator for Italy's telecoms market, AN leader Gianfranco Fini said in a statement on Thursday.

The draft law, which has been delayed for months, ran into more trouble earlier this week when a parliamentary commission abandoned work on it in the face over some 6,400 amendments and sub-amendments.

The watchdog, which will regulate the privatised telecoms and television sectors, must be set up before the sell-off of the state's 64 percent holding in telecoms holding Stet, which the government wants to take place by March 31 next year.

Fini said in his statement: "To make clear to everybody that AN is in favour of privatisations and in particular that of Stet, senator Riccardo De Corato will withdraw all (our) obstructionist amendments."
Parliamentary sources said this concerned more than 2,000 amendments.

"For AN the problem is not the privatisation of Stet but the readiness of the coalition to satisfy Communist Refoundation, which is against privatisations and impeding every reasonable hypothesis and fair solution to questions relating to the reordering of the broadcast sector and to the introduction of anti-trust regulations," Fini said.

The far-left Communist Refoundation, the party Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left coalition relies on for a majority in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house), has presented nearly 100 amendments of its own to the bill.
It is ideolgically opposed to the sell-off of Stet.

Italy is under pressure to complete the Stet sale in order to honour promises to the European Union under a deal which allowed it to bail out a bankrupt state holding company if it sold Stet by the end of the year.
Brussels has already given Rome a six month extension on the Stet sale, but the government is increasingly alarmed that even this new timetable might prove impossible.
